name: The lower thread that loops and snaps
subject: repair
brief: In the craft room before sports day, you are hemming cotton house-team armbands on the cast-iron treadle sewing machine. It stitches a clean six-inch run, then suddenly bunches loops underneath and snaps the lower thread. The house captains are waiting outside the door for the armbands.

causes.name: Lint wedged between the upper tension discs lets the needle thread slacken
A tiny needle-strike burr on the lip of the steel bobbin case catches the shuttle thread every few turns
The needle eye is rough and frays the cotton on the downstroke
The wooden top spool is cross-wound and jerks on its upright pin

tests.name: Open the slide plate and inspect the upper discs and bobbin-case lip under the bench lamp
Run a thumbnail along the bobbin-case slot and down the needle point
Pull both threads through a small spring gauge to compare upper and needle-eye drag
Hold the bobbin case by its thread tail and gauge whether it jerks and catches as it unwinds
Fit a fresh mercerised cotton reel from the workbox onto the top spool pin

note: Set in the craft room at Nabapara Vidyalaya (loc_nhss). A needle-strike burr on the lip of the bobbin case catches the lower thread every few turns, so the fault comes and goes. Opening the slide plate and running a thumbnail along the case lip isolates it.
